quote: Was braucht die Physik zu ihrer befriedigenden logischen Be- gründung?
english: What does physics need for its satisfactory logical foundation?
topic: Hilbert reflects on modern mathematics, which seeks inner understanding through ideas and culminates in the axiomatic method, and then asks what physics needs from mathematics for its progress and for its logical foundation.

triage.modern_statement: This is Hilbert's program for axiomatizing physics. It became the 6th of his 1900 problems: find axioms for the physical theories, especially probability and mechanics, as rigorous as the axioms of geometry, and derive the theories logically from them. This includes deriving macroscopic laws, such as fluid and continuum equations, from microscopic mechanics by way of Boltzmann's kinetic theory. The note is a broad programmatic question, not one precise theorem. In modern terms it amounts to mathematical physics as a whole: rigorous axiomatic foundations for quantum mechanics, quantum field theory, statistical mechanics and general relativity, plus rigorous derivations that link one level of description to the next.
triage.answered_by: There is no complete answer. It is Hilbert's 6th problem (Paris, 1900), and Hilbert himself kept working on it in lectures from about 1898 to 1918 (Leo Corry, 2004). Some parts have been solved. A recent landmark is Yu Deng, Zaher Hani and Xiao Ma (arXiv:2503.01800, March 2025). They rigorously derived the Euler and Navier–Stokes fluid equations from Newtonian hard-sphere particle dynamics via the Boltzmann equation. That settles the Boltzmann-program part of the problem. Commentators say the problem as a whole is still open.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's sixth problem is the axiomatisation of physics. The first six of his 1900 problems concern foundations, including the foundations of physics.
The sixth problem of the 1900 list is a programmatic call to axiomatize the physical sciences. It grew out of Hilbert's foundational work on geometry.
Leo Corry's book 'David Hilbert and the Axiomatization of Physics (1898-1918)' traces Hilbert's long work on axiomatizing physics in his Göttingen lectures.

Deng, Hani and Ma (2025) derived the fluid equations from particle dynamics via Boltzmann's kinetic theory. They say this resolves the sixth problem as it pertains to Hilbert's program for that question, and that broadly read the problem covers all of modern mathematical physics.
One commentary argues that the Deng–Hani–Ma work advances only a narrow front and that the sixth problem remains open in full generality.

triage.why: The page context (the axiomatic method as the high point of modern mathematics, and what physics needs from mathematics for its logical foundation) matches Hilbert's 6th problem and his wider program for axiomatizing physics, as documented by Corry. I can't tell from the sources which year this diary entry was written or how it relates to the 1900 lecture, and the note itself states no specific theorem. That is why the verdict is 'known_published_problem' rather than 'solved'. Some parts have been solved, most notably the 2025 particle-to-Boltzmann-to-fluid derivation, and research on it is clearly active (2025–2026 arXiv papers). Full axiomatization of physics, quantum field theory for example, is still open.
